Reproducibility in `readfiscalnz` has two parts: selecting the exact
publication and retaining the exact bytes parsed. This article explains the
static release catalogue, source terms, provenance fields, raw snapshots, and
the in-memory parsed-result cache. It uses a packaged synthetic CSV fixture;
no network request is made while the article is built.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(readfiscalnz)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)

hfi_file <- system.file("extdata", "hfi.csv", package = "readfiscalnz")
if (!nzchar(hfi_file)) {
  stop("The installed hfi.csv fixture is unavailable.")
}

cache <- tempfile("readfiscalnz-provenance-")
dir.create(cache, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Start with the release catalogue

`list_nz_fiscal_releases()` is an offline catalogue, not a discovery scraper.
It records six supported release identities, their family, publication status,
official landing and artifact URLs, expected SHA-256, and revision note.

Those rows do not all represent the same kind of coverage. The HFI and tax
rows each identify one published snapshot of a rolling, revised history; the
monthly financials row identifies one eight-month reporting snapshot; and the
three EFU rows identify three separate vintages containing actual or unaudited
and forecast rows. The catalogue is therefore neither a complete Treasury
dataset index nor a complete archive of every publication vintage.

```{r catalogue}
catalogue <- list_nz_fiscal_releases()
stopifnot(nrow(catalogue) == 6L)

catalogue[c(
  "release_id", "family", "release_type", "status", "issue_date",
  "expected_sha256", "revision_note"
)]
```

Selecting `release_id` is preferable when an analysis must be replayed later.
With no explicit identifier, the `as_published` revision policy (the default)
selects the newest current catalogue row and falls back to the newest issue
date when that family has no current row; `latest` always selects the newest
issue date. The selected policy and release are recorded in provenance.

## Review the source terms

Terms are also static package metadata. `nz_fiscal_terms()` does not fetch a
page, grant permission, or write to a cache. It gives the links and attribution
needed for a human review before enabling a live read.

```{r terms}
terms <- nz_fiscal_terms("hfi-1972-2025")
stopifnot(
  nrow(terms) == 1L,
  identical(terms$terms_license, "CC BY 4.0"),
  identical(terms$terms_attribution, "The Treasury")
)

terms[c(
  "release_id", "terms_statement", "terms_license", "terms_attribution",
  "license_url", "terms_url", "terms_verified_at"
)]
```

The package records the Treasury statement and links but does not provide legal
advice. Third-party material on an official page may have separate rights;
the package routes only the catalogued Treasury data artifacts. The installed
terms record at `system.file("TERMS.md", package = "readfiscalnz")` documents
the boundary and complete links.

## Local replay versus official retrieval

Supplying `file` is the reproducible offline route. The file is checked for a
supported extension and signature, copied to a content-addressed raw snapshot,
and parsed through the normal validation path. The input file is not modified
and no network request is made. A local replay records `source_kind =
"local_file"` and preserves both the actual input hash and the selected
release's catalogue hash.

```{r local-provenance}
hfi <- read_nz_hfi(
  release_id = "hfi-1972-2025",
  file = hfi_file,
  sheets = "Spending",
  cache_dir = cache
)
provenance <- nz_fiscal_provenance(hfi)

stopifnot(
  identical(provenance$source_kind, "local_file"),
  identical(provenance$revision_policy, "as_published"),
  nchar(provenance$raw_sha256) == 64L,
  nchar(provenance$catalogue_sha256) == 64L,
  file.exists(provenance$raw_snapshot_path)
)

data.frame(
  field = c("source_kind", "release_id", "raw_size_bytes", "raw_sha256",
            "catalogue_sha256", "parser_version", "schema_version"),
  value = c(
    provenance$source_kind,
    provenance$release_id,
    as.character(provenance$raw_size_bytes),
    substr(provenance$raw_sha256, 1L, 16L),
    substr(provenance$catalogue_sha256, 1L, 16L),
    provenance$parser_version,
    provenance$schema_version
  ),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

The installed CSV is a synthetic example, so its `raw_sha256` is intentionally
different from the official workbook hash in `catalogue_sha256`. This is an
explicit fixture trust boundary, not a claim that the fixture is an official
release. An official download is accepted only after transport, size,
signature, HTTPS-host, and catalogue SHA-256 checks succeed.

With `file = NULL`, the live route first resolves the catalogued official URL
but may reuse an existing exact hash-addressed raw-cache entry rather than
transfer the bytes again. The live equivalent is conditional so routine builds
remain offline:

```{r live-source}
if (identical(Sys.getenv("READFISCALNZ_LIVE"), "true")) {
  official <- read_nz_hfi(
    release_id = "hfi-1972-2025",
    accept_terms = TRUE,
    cache_dir = tempfile("readfiscalnz-official-cache-"),
    timeout_sec = 30
  )
  nz_fiscal_provenance(official)[
    c("source_kind", "resolved_url", "raw_sha256", "catalogue_sha256")
  ]
}
```

## Verify and replay the exact bytes

`nz_fiscal_raw_bytes()` reads the archived bytes only after confirming that the
snapshot still exists, remains within `max_bytes`, and has the recorded
SHA-256. It never downloads a replacement.

```{r raw-bytes}
raw <- nz_fiscal_raw_bytes(hfi)
raw_hash <- digest::digest(raw, algo = "sha256", serialize = FALSE)

stopifnot(
  is.raw(raw),
  identical(raw_hash, provenance$raw_sha256),
  length(raw) == provenance$raw_size_bytes
)

c(raw_bytes = length(raw), sha256_matches = identical(raw_hash, provenance$raw_sha256))
```

The `raw_snapshot_path` is useful to a local auditor, while `raw_sha256` is
the portable identity to record in an analysis manifest. Do not rely on a
temporary path surviving another machine or R session.

## Understand the two cache layers

There are two separate caches:

* The raw cache contains immutable, hash-addressed `.xlsx` or `.csv` snapshots
  below `cache_dir/raw`. It is persistent and bounded by file-count, total-byte,
  and age settings.
* The parsed cache is an in-memory LRU cache for the current R process. Its key
  includes the raw hash, release, revision policy, parser version, schema
  version, and parser options. It does not replace the raw snapshot.

The default raw cache is
`tools::R_user_dir("readfiscalnz", "cache")/v1`. A project, test, or vignette
can supply `cache_dir` directly; the `readfiscalnz.cache_dir` option changes
the default for a session. The other policy options are
`readfiscalnz.parsed_cache_entries`, `readfiscalnz.raw_cache_files`,
`readfiscalnz.raw_cache_bytes`, `readfiscalnz.raw_cache_max_age_days`, and
`readfiscalnz.download_attempts` (the last controls live retries, up to three).

The following local option block demonstrates an isolated policy and restores
the caller's options when it exits. It does not change the package defaults.

```{r cache-options}
local({
  old <- options(
    readfiscalnz.cache_dir = cache,
    readfiscalnz.parsed_cache_entries = 4L,
    readfiscalnz.raw_cache_files = 8L,
    readfiscalnz.raw_cache_bytes = 5 * 1024^2,
    readfiscalnz.raw_cache_max_age_days = 30,
    readfiscalnz.download_attempts = 2L
  )
  on.exit(options(old), add = TRUE)

  replay <- read_nz_hfi(
    release_id = "hfi-1972-2025",
    file = hfi_file,
    sheets = "Spending"
  )
  stopifnot(identical(nrow(replay), nrow(hfi)))
  c(
    parsed_entries = getOption("readfiscalnz.parsed_cache_entries"),
    raw_files = getOption("readfiscalnz.raw_cache_files"),
    raw_bytes = getOption("readfiscalnz.raw_cache_bytes"),
    raw_max_age_days = getOption("readfiscalnz.raw_cache_max_age_days"),
    download_attempts = getOption("readfiscalnz.download_attempts")
  )
})
```

Use `prune_nz_fiscal_cache()` for explicit local maintenance. It only removes
managed raw snapshots and never makes a network request; pass `preserve` when
an in-use snapshot must survive the pruning pass.

```{r prune}
pruned <- prune_nz_fiscal_cache(
  cache_dir = cache,
  max_files = 1L,
  max_bytes = 5 * 1024^2,
  max_age_days = Inf,
  preserve = provenance$raw_snapshot_path
)
stopifnot(identical(names(pruned), c("files", "bytes")))
pruned
```

## What provenance does and does not guarantee

Provenance records the release identity, source route, source location,
snapshot path and size, actual raw hash, catalogue hash, terms metadata,
revision policy, parser version, schema version, and parser options. It does
not infer that two releases are comparable merely because their display names
match. Use `nz_fiscal_series_catalogue()` to make structural identity explicit,
and retain the provenance list with any derived output.

The package currently fails closed on an unsupported release, missing or
changed workbook structure, invalid signature, size limit, or official hash
drift. It does not silently download during package load, tests, or local
replay. `accept_terms = TRUE` is required only for the live route and is not a
credential. The troubleshooting vignette maps these failures to recovery
actions.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(cache, recursive = TRUE)
```
